about: Parameters for the target-density canary sheet. The 160 rings, 1,740 landform instances and 340 labels are GENERATED from `seed` by an integer hash in tools/mapforge/lib/synthetic-sheet.mjs, not committed — half a megabyte of fixture nobody reads is not a fixture. What is committed is the parameter set and the census it must hit, so the sheet is reviewable on one screen and reproducible byte for byte.

paramsWhy.frameKm/pxPerKm: 400 km at 3.5 px/km is the ATLAS SHEET'S OWN frame, 1400 x 1400 px — the canary is only evidence about the real chart if it is the real chart's size. content/world/budgets.json's maxSvgBytes rationale is measured at exactly this frame.
paramsWhy.glyphSizePx: GLYPH_SIZE.min. Declared here rather than hardcoded so checkGlyphSizes is what stops a future re-census picking a small size to make 1,740 marks fit — the size contract wins and the layout accommodates it, not the other way round.
paramsWhy.instances: All 1,740 are drawn as FAMILY-SPECIFIC marks at GLYPH_SIZE.min. The live world will draw ~340 named marks and leave the rest as texture; a canary that did the same would be measuring an easier sheet than the one it is meant to warn about.

rankMix.about: Labels per RANKS key, summing to `params.labels`. NOT a uniform draw: a uniform mix over nine ranks would put ~38 labels at rank 0-1, where the font is 15 px, and none of the 160 region names that actually crowd a world chart. This mirrors the world Plan C will generate — one name per region, one capital per landmass — so the declutter is exercised on the real shape of the problem. Low rank means HIGH priority and a BIGGER box, so a mix cannot be made easy by tilting it downward either way; it is made honest by matching the census.
